On Adreno GPUs the game can run on another Vulkan driver than the system\'s, for example a Mesa Turnip build or a newer Qualcomm driver. Use driver packages in the AdrenoTools format (a .zip with meta.json and the driver), as other emulators use them. A new driver applies after a restart. If the game doesn\'t start with it, the next start goes back to the system driver.

Why none: Android hands a controller\'s motion sensors to apps only when the device\'s Linux kernel drives the controller with its own driver, for this one %1$s. This device\'s kernel (%2$s) has none for it, so the controller runs as a plain HID gamepad: buttons and sticks work, but Android makes no motion sensors of it (no \"Motion Sensors\" input device). An app can\'t get past that: over Bluetooth the system keeps the controller\'s raw data to itself. A system update or a kernel with the driver (on a custom ROM: ask its maker) brings them; until then motion controls use this device\'s sensors.

Why none: Android hands a controller\'s rumble motors to apps only when the device\'s Linux kernel drives the controller with its own driver, for this one %1$s. This device\'s kernel (%2$s) has none for it, so the controller runs as a plain HID gamepad: buttons and sticks work, but Android gets no rumble (force feedback) for it. An app can\'t get past that: over Bluetooth the system keeps the controller to itself. A system update or a kernel with the driver (on a custom ROM: ask its maker) brings it; until then this device rumbles.
Why none: Android hands a controller\'s motion sensors to apps from Android 12 on; this device has Android %1$s. Motion controls use this device\'s sensors.

Every enemy: ZL stays on, also with none in reach, and locks each enemy that comes in reach; a nearer enemy takes over the lock. For ZL tapped or held
How the picture is enlarged to the screen: Sharp keeps edges crisp at lower rendering resolutions, Pixel perfect shows each rendered pixel as a crisp block
Go to any place, room and spawn point of the game

Imports mods from .zip, .rar and .7z files: Cemu graphic packs (for example from GameBanana or GitHub) and plain game file mods (a content folder). Code patches (patch_*.asm), game file replacements, pixel shader replacements and texture filtering rules work; vertex shaders and texture resolution rules don\'t yet. A code patch only applies to the game version it was made for. Turning packs on or off, or changing their settings, takes effect after a restart.
Delete this pack from the device?
Top loads first. Where packs change the same game file, shader or code, the lower one wins. Drag ≡ to move a pack; with a controller pick it up with A and move it up or down.
Each save file has its own packs, presets and loading order. Choosing a file with other packs restarts the game with them
The packs below are this save file\'s
The game runs with File %1$d\'s packs now. Another file\'s changes need no restart: they load when you choose that file.
File %1$d\'s mod packs are on now. Choose File %1$d again to play it.
File %1$d uses other mod packs. Restart the game with them now? Cancel goes back to the file select.
Loading File %1$d with its mod packs…
Moving: up / down, press again to put it down
Patch groups: %1$d for this game version, %2$d for others
Pick one or more .zip, .rar or .7z files; also GameCube player models (a model pack with a Link.arc, made for the GameCube randomizer): they are converted for HD
Converted from a GameCube player model. Choose it for a save file on the player models page
Converted from a GameCube player model by %1$s. Choose it for a save file on the player models page
Who each save file plays as: Link or one of the %1$d imported models
Models imported from GameCube custom model packs. Each save file plays as its own: pick the file, then the model. It changes in the game at once, no restart; randomized games too.
Each save file has its own model; it changes as soon as that file is played
Making room: player models from before keep only what they need…
Changes apply after a restart; changed code is then recompiled (a short compile, or none for a combination used before).

After turning on a pack that patches code, start from the title screen once and load your quest log there: the pack sets itself up while the game loads. Save states made without the pack don\'t have it set up.

A preset is the story part of a save (items, hearts, songs, chart, each place\'s switches and chests, story flags) plus a place. Warping to it loads that story into the game you are playing; your save file only changes if you save in the game. Presets stay on this device.
%1$s\n\nWarp there with this story? It replaces the story of the game you are playing until you load your save again.
Load the story of a save file or a saved moment and warp to its place
The story just before a song is learned, Link right in front of its stone tablet or teacher

Each loads the built-in story preset from just before that song is learned and puts Link in front of where the game teaches it (a stone tablet, Tott). Read the tablet or talk to the teacher, then take out the Wind Waker when the game asks for the song.
Pick a WWHD cking.sav, GameCube .gci saves (USA, Europe, Japan) or presets (.wwp); several at once: each used slot becomes a preset
Save the current story as a preset
Here and now: the story so far and the place you entered
Controller: D-pad moves · right button selects · bottom button starts the game
Takes Link to the place at once, as a door would. The story stays as in your save file: who and what is there depends on it (or pick a layer). Save in the game only if you want to keep the new place.
Which version of the place loads; Story picks it from your progress
Reading the places from your game files… (a few seconds, only this once)
A panel over the game: ✓ / ✗ rate the spot and warp to the next; results in warp_tests.tsv

resources.string:
The game files were not found or don't match this build.

This app contains only the recompiled code built from your own copy of the game; it needs the extracted game files from the same dump. Extract them on a computer (see README.md: tools/wudextract.py), then copy the resulting folder (with code/, content/ and meta/ inside) to:

%1$s

For example: adb push game /sdcard/Android/data/org.wwhdrecomp.app/files/

Problem: %2$s

Welcome!

This app contains no game files. It plays your own copy of The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD for Wii U (USA, European or Japanese version).

Put these three files on this device, then choose them together:
• your disc image (.wux or .wud)
• its disc key (the image's name with .key)
• the console's common key (common.key)

Or choose a Cemu archive of your game (.wua); it needs no keys.

The app then extracts the game files (about 1.7 GB) and prepares the game code for this device. That happens once and takes a while, depending on the device's processor.
The game files found don\'t work: %1$s
Extract from your disc image or .wua…

Choose your disc image, its disc key and the console\'s common key together (long-press the first, then tap the others):
%1$s the image (.wux or .wud) %2$s its disc key (the image\'s name with .key) %3$s common.key
Or a Cemu archive of your game (.wua).
If the picker doesn\'t show your files, put them directly into Download and open Downloads there.
A key file must hold 16 bytes or 32 hex digits.
Extracting the game from your disc image…
This step needs about %1$d MB of free storage; %2$d MB are free. Free up some space and try again.

Preparing the game code for this device…\n\nThis happens once and takes a while, depending on this device\'s processor: a few minutes on fast devices, longer on slower ones. You can leave the app meanwhile: it continues in the background (see the notification), and if it is closed, it continues where it stopped.
Dividing the game code into parts (%1$d:%2$02d)
Preparing the game code was cancelled. It continues where it stopped when you start again.

Choose a backup made with Export (WindWakerHD backup ….zip), a GameCube Wind Waker save (.gci, USA, Europe or Japan: it becomes your game save, all three quest logs), or the files themselves together (long-press the first, then tap the others): cking.sav with the other cking….sav files of a game save, slot1–5.bin and .png of save states. If the picker doesn\'t show them, put the files directly into Download and open Downloads there.
GameCube save %1$s, converted: all three quest logs
No game save (cking.sav) or save states (slot1–5.bin) among the files picked.
Save states imported. States from another build of the app can\'t be loaded.
Game save imported. The game restarts now to use it (the previous save is kept in save-before-import).

Lossless.dll is installed and frame generation is on, but this version of its shaders hasn\'t been tested with the app: generated frames may look wrong. If they do, select another Lossless.dll (the README names the tested one).

On this GPU (%1$s), frame generation can make the GPU hang. The game may crash, and in rare cases the whole device may freeze or restart.\n\nIf the game crashes, the dialog at its next start offers to start without frame generation.
Lossless.dll is ready and frame generation is on.
Drag to move · tap elsewhere when done

A short test (about 2 minutes) finds the graphics settings for this device. The game starts for it, but its picture stays hidden and there is no sound. Your saves are not touched. Afterwards you choose whether to use the result.
Frame generation: if you own Lossless Scaling (Steam) and want frame generation, choose its Lossless.dll now, so the test includes it.
It stopped at: %1$s. Your settings stay as they were. You can run it again under Options > Graphics.
the app left the screen (screen off or another app) while measuring
%1$s: 60 fps, rendering resolution up to %2$s× (lowered when needed)
%1$s: 30 fps, rendering resolution up to %2$s× (lowered when needed)
%1$s with frame generation: 30 fps doubled to 60, rendering resolution up to %2$s× (lowered when needed)
Frame generation didn\'t reach 60 fps on this device, so the recommendation is without it.
The game stopped while the test tried frame generation, so it is not recommended on this device.
Patches the game code of this game version
Made for another game version: does nothing here
Your mod pack changes only take effect after a restart. Restart the game now? Progress since your last save is lost.
The game uses the new language after a restart.
The menus use the new language after a restart.
Finding the game\'s shaders in your game files… (only this once)
No used Wind Waker save slots found in this file
Loaded; Auto waits for the cutscene / dialogue to end (at most 20 s)
Warp, or rate and go on with ✓ / ✗
No end after %1$.0f s: stuck. Restart the app (it is written down and skipped).
Not taken: a scene change was under way. Tap Warp again.
Applied once a save file is loaded; save in the game to keep it.
The setting applies after a restart.
The driver package couldn\'t be installed: %1$s
this is not a driver package (a .zip with meta.json and the driver\'s .so file)
%1$s is installed. Use it now? The game restarts.

The game closed last time because the phone's GPU driver hung:
%1$s

This can happen with buggy system drivers. A Turnip driver usually runs the game. Choose a driver package (a .zip in the AdrenoTools format, e.g. a recent Turnip build for your Adreno) to use it from now on, or start the game as it is.

The game closed last time because the installed GPU driver hung:
%1$s

Go back to the system driver, choose another driver package, or start the game with this one again.
Switch to %1$s? The game restarts; the first start with another driver compiles its pipelines again and takes longer.
This driver is in use. Remove it and restart with the system driver?
The game didn\'t start with the GPU driver %1$s, so it runs on the system driver again. You can choose the driver again under Graphics › GPU driver.

A crash log was saved. If you report the problem (for example as an issue on GitHub), please attach it. It shows where the game crashed, the app version, the game version, your device model and the settings in use. It contains no personal data.
The game log could not be collected.

Collects this game\'s log of the current run, with what is needed to reproduce a problem: app and game version, device, GPU and driver, and the settings. Only this app\'s own lines are taken, nothing of other apps. Nothing personal is contained: no names or accounts, and folder paths, links, email, network and Bluetooth addresses and device IDs are left out. The zip then goes where you choose in the share menu.\n\nWith the switch on, the save files are added too: your progress as last saved in the game, the pictos and the album pages. The name you gave Link becomes \"Link\" in that copy; your own save stays as it is.

The game restarts without its shader cache, as on the first start: shaders are compiled again as scenes appear, so the first visit to each scene loads slower and may stutter. Saves, save states and settings stay. (Unsaved progress is lost.)
Drag to move (locks on the grid while Grid is on), pinch or Size to resize, tap to select.
Opacity: only the selected control (tap an empty spot for all)
Opacity: all controls (tap a control for only that one)
No saved layouts yet. Save current keeps the layout you are editing under a name.
A layout for the %1$s touch controls. Load puts it into the editor; Done keeps it.
A saved layout of this style already has this name. Replace it?
This layout is for the %1$s touch controls. Load it and switch the touch controls to %1$s?
Flexible layout: the sticks appear where your thumbs land
The bow, boomerang, hookshot and grappling hook with the context buttons. Tap: a tap aims, then the button shoots with each tap, ZL switches the view, B puts the item away. Hold: as in the game

With Item buttons: Tap, while an item is aimed only its Shoot button, B (put away), ZL and ZR (arrow types) show; the other item buttons, A, +, first person, the d-pad and the jump buttons hide, so no stray tap lets go of a drawn arrow

With Context buttons, once Link stands still the sword and any other item in his hand (Skull Hammer, boomerang...) go away 5 s after the last swing and the Deku Leaf after 3 s; with Item buttons: Tap also the telescope and the Picto Box when their view closes, and an aimed item on B; A\'s Put away hides. Off: they stay in Link\'s hand (B while aiming only goes back) and A puts them away, as in the game. At first on with Item buttons: Tap, off with Hold
While Link holds the Wind Waker, sing, hum or whistle one of its songs into the microphone and he plays it (only songs he has learned). The sound is only analysed, never recorded

Hold the mic button at the bottom left (or L on a controller) while singing; letting go plays the song at once. The switch below it picks the time (3/4, 4/4, 6/4): while you hold the button, Link conducts the notes you sing, one per beat of the metronome. Off: the microphone listens by itself and a short pause ends a song
Play buttons in the song list
While Link holds the baton, + shows the songs he knows: a play button beside each one plays it at once, no conducting needed
When the story waits for one song (learning it at a stone tablet, a sage), a play button on the message box plays it at once, learned or not
Hold the mic button and sing
Without the microphone permission the songs can\'t be heard. You can allow it in the system settings of the app.
A new game with the items in other places (TWWHD Randomizer)

The randomizer (TWWHD Randomizer 1.2.0 by SuperDude88 and others) makes a new game from yours: the items are in other places, the sea is open from the start, most cutscenes are gone. Its logic makes sure every game can be finished. The randomized game has its own game save and save states; the game as it is stays as it is.
The randomizer can\'t use these game files: an unknown version of the game.
Switching between the randomized game and the game as it is then needs no compile. Costs about 60 MB more (all compiled code now: %1$d MB).
Seed hash %1$s (seed %2$s): the game\'s title screen shows the same words. With its save and save states: %3$d MB.
Where every item is. Only if you are stuck!
The spoiler log can\'t be read.
Seed hash %1$s. Everything below tells where things are: look only when you are stuck.
Each item at its place on the sea chart and in the dungeons
The order in which the important items can be got
Each step needs only the items of the steps before it (and the starting items).
Every place\'s item, by island and dungeon
The items on the way through; the rest are rupees and other small things
The randomizer\'s whole log, to read or share

A preset replaces all settings below (the seed name too).

Beginner: fewer places to search, hints, normal damage.
Standard: the randomizer's own settings.
Everything: items in almost every place.
Which kinds of places can hold the items you need
Places that are off only have rupees and other minor things, so you never have to search them.
Race mode: only the dungeons you must finish hold important items
Where keys, maps and compasses are
For Race mode (Places): how many dungeons are needed to reach Ganon\'s Tower
Doors and caves that lead somewhere else
Shuffled entrances lead into other dungeons, caves or rooms. This makes a game much harder to find your way in.
Who tells you where things are
Hearts at the start, swords, damage
Pieces of Heart at the start
Link never gets a sword (only for experienced players)
× 2 is the randomizer\'s standard, × 1 as in the game
Faster text, the whole sea chart and more
The same seed and settings make the same game
All settings and the seed in one text: share it, or paste one from the PC randomizer
The randomizer\'s own settings and a new seed
A new game will be made at the next start.

The app restarts and makes a new game with these settings (a few seconds), then the game code is compiled again (the first randomized game: all of it, as long as the first start; a later one: only the changed parts) and the new game starts.\n\nThe games you have stay, each with its own save; at each start the app asks which one to play. A randomized game takes about half a gigabyte.
%1$s was made with these settings and this seed: it would be the same game again. Make one with a new seed?
At each start the app asks which one to play. Each randomized game has its own save and save states.
Which game do you want to play?
You are playing this game now.
This randomized game is deleted. The game as it is and the other randomized games stay.
This randomized game is deleted with its game save and save states. The game as it is and the other randomized games stay.
You are playing this game: it is deleted with its game save and save states, and the app restarts with the game as it is.
His clothes, hair and eyes in other colours, or his casual clothes from the start
These colours go into the next randomized game made. A game made already gets them with “Make it again with Link\'s colours” on its page: the same game, with its save and save states.
A new file starts in Link\'s casual clothes instead of the hero\'s (the colours here are those clothes\')
His clothes, hair and eyes in other colours in the game (randomized games have their own)
In the game as it is, for this save file; randomized games keep the colours they were made with

Save file %1$d plays as the player model %2$s, which keeps its own colours: Link\'s colours can\'t be set for it. To colour Link in this file, choose Link (none) for it under Mods > Mod packs > GameCube player model.
Link wears his island clothes and then the hero\'s: each has its own colours. Skin, mouth and eyes are the same in both unless Own skin, mouth and eyes is on.
Whose colours are shown and changed here
Off: one colour for both clothes. On: each clothes its own, changed along with Link\'s clothes
The same in both clothes (Own skin, mouth and eyes: each their own)
Each save file has its own colours; changes show in the game at once
A randomized game is played now: it has its own colours. These show in the game as it is.
Give a save file another name in play, up to 16 characters
Whose name is shown and changed here

The game uses the new name at once; save in the game to keep it. Up to %1$d characters: the game itself keeps the first %2$d in its save, and the file select shows those. This app keeps the rest and puts the whole name back whenever that file is played. Text boxes wrap a line earlier with a long name.
The names come from the game: start it (load a save file) to change one.
The game has no letter \"%1$s\". Please use other letters.
Make it again with Link\'s colours
At a restart, this game is made again with the colours on Randomizer > Link\'s colours. Everything else stays: the same items in the same places, its save and save states.
%1$s will be made again with Link\'s colours at the next start.
The randomizer could not make the game:\n\n%1$s
Play the game as it is
The map of where things are found is off in the randomized game: it shows where the game itself has them.

resources.string: On a TV: you play with a game controller (Bluetooth or USB); the remote works in the menus. If this TV has no file chooser, copy the files into this folder (with adb push, or a file manager allowed there) and choose “Use the files in the app\'s folder”:\n%1$s
Use the files in the app\'s folder

The folder is empty. Copy your disc image with its two keys, or a Cemu archive (.wua), into:
%1$s

For example from a computer: adb push MyGame.wua %1$s/
This device has no file chooser for apps (common on TVs). Install a file manager that offers one, or copy the files into this folder with adb push:\n%1$s
Phones, tablets and TVs together in the same Wi-Fi: one runs the game, the others are its GamePad or its screen

One device runs the game, the others join it in the same Wi-Fi.

The game here, the picture on a TV or tablet: switch on “Others can join this device” below. Then on the TV or tablet: Game > Other devices > Be another device's screen.

The game on a TV, this device as the GamePad: Play on another screen.

A device without the game joins straight away: long press the app icon (GamePad or Screen), or the buttons on its setup screen.

One device runs the game, the others join it in the same Wi-Fi.

The game here, a phone or tablet as the GamePad: leave “Others can join this device” on. On the phone: Game > Other devices > Play on another screen, or long press the app icon > GamePad.

The game on a phone, this TV as its screen: on the phone switch on Game > Other devices > “Others can join this device”, then choose Be another device's screen here.
This device runs the game: phones, tablets and TVs with the app in the same Wi-Fi find it and become its GamePad or its screen. On by default on a TV.
This device becomes the GamePad of a TV, phone or tablet running this app in the same network: that one shows the game, this screen the GamePad\'s. Your saves go along.
The game here closes (saved as with Quit), and this device looks for TVs, phones and tablets running the app in your network.
Looking for devices running the app in this network…
On the other device: the app open, Game > Other devices > Others can join this device on, and both in the same Wi-Fi.
The TV\'s address in the network (for example 192.168.1.20), if it isn\'t found by itself:
Stop looking and go back to the start?
The connection to the other device is lost. Trying again…
Type the code the other device shows:
Wrong code. Type the code the other device shows:
The TV has another version of the app. Install the same version on both.
Connected to %1$s. The picture comes as soon as the game runs there.
Send this device\'s game files (%1$s) to %2$s? It then prepares the game, which takes a while.
This device has no game files to send either.
%1$s has only %2$s of free storage: save states (%3$s) stay on this device, the rest goes along now. Free up storage there to bring them too.
%1$s has only %2$s of free storage, about %3$s are needed: nothing was sent. Free up storage there and connect again.
%1$s prepares the game. The picture comes as soon as it runs.
Your saves are on %1$s: it restarts with them…
Bring the saves back when I leave
%1$s wants to be the GamePad. Type this code on it: %2$s
The game files could not be put in place.
The saves from the phone are here: the game restarts.

The size the other device sends the GamePad picture in (now: %1$s). Larger is sharper but asks more of both devices and the network. None: this device is a controller only; the other device keeps the GamePad picture (+ shows it there) and sends nothing.
Drawn here, the game\'s own screens as video
The items show here once the game runs there.
Your journey so far: %1$d%%. Tap a thing for its name.
The GamePad picture stays on the TV: + shows it there.

The other device plays the %1$s release of the game, this one the %2$s release. The game save goes along all the same (made fit for the other release); save states can\'t: they belong to one release\'s game, so they stay where they are.

The game here closes (saved as with Quit), and this device looks for a device running the app in your network to be its screen: it shows the game and plays its sound, the other one plays and shows the GamePad.
The size the other device sends the game picture in (now: %1$s). Larger is sharper but asks more of the network.

This device shows the game of a phone or tablet running this app in the same network (and plays its sound): that one runs the game, shows the GamePad and is the controller. For a weak device with a large screen.
Delay: picture %1$s ms, network round trip %2$s ms, sound %3$s ms

Send this device\'s game files (%1$s) to %2$s? This device first prepares the game code for its processor (a few minutes here), so %2$s can start the game right away instead of preparing it itself, which takes much longer there.
Preparing the game code for %1$s: %2$d of %3$d
Or without any game files here: choose “Be another device\'s screen”. A phone or tablet with the app and your game then runs it and is the GamePad; this TV shows the game and plays its sound.
Game picture there (TV by cast or cable)

%1$s is preparing the game code for its processor itself, which can take long there (on a TV box up to an hour). This device can do it in a few minutes and send it; %1$s then starts the game. Prepare it here?
How do you want to play now?
The game runs on this device.
Another device runs the game, this one is its GamePad.
This device shows the game of a phone or tablet that joins it.
This page comes at every start: Game > Other devices > Choose at the start.

On the phone or tablet with the game: Game > Other devices > Show on a TV, then pick this device. Or this one finds it here once Others can join this device is on there (both in the same Wi-Fi): the first device found is joined.
Each start of the app asks first: play here, be another device\'s GamePad, or wait for a device and be its screen.
%1$s wants to be this device\'s screen. Type this code on it: %2$s
Pick a TV or tablet waiting to be the screen (the screen app open there, or Be another device\'s screen): it shows the game and plays its sound, this device stays the GamePad. No code to type.
Looking for screens in this Wi-Fi… On the TV: the screen app open (or Game > Other devices > Be another device\'s screen there).
These are waiting to be the screen. Pick one: it joins this device.
%1$s didn\'t answer. Is its search page still open?
